content:
Maria K: Heads up — in ap-northeast-1 our ALB is flapping and launcher pods can't finish init. Health checks failing on backend targets.
Devon: seeing same. ALB shows 503 from target, target group 'gpu-nodes-prod' marked unhealthy.
Maria K: Quick grep of security group shows backend-sg has inbound 8443 from prefix-list:pl-0a1b2c but healthchecks come from ALB SG not internet — maybe we used wrong source when creating rule.
Linh: can you paste the SG rule?
Maria K: ```Inbound: Type: HTTPS, Protocol: TCP, PortRange: 8443, Source: pl-0a1b2c (arn:aws:ec2:ap-northeast-1:123456789012:prefix-list/pl-0a1b2c)```
Ashok: That prefix-list is our artifact registry egress PL, not the ALB. ALB SG id is sg-0b2c3d — rule should reference sg-0b2c3d not the prefix-list.
Devon: Confirmed. ALB healthcheck uses client IP from ALB SG so backend must allow ALB SG. Also outbound from nodes to S3 works via NAT — but NACL denies high ephemeral ports in that subnet, so node pulls fail intermittently.
Maria K: NACL shows DENY for 32768-65535 outbound on the app-subnet. wtf.
Ashok: looks like a terraform change last night tightened NACL. Rolling back to allow ephemeral range 1024-65535 outbound fixes S3 pulls.
Linh: Proposed immediate actions: 1) add SG rule allowing sg-0b2c3d -> 8443, 2) relax NACL outbound ephemeral ports, 3) force re-register targets or restart kube-proxy.
Devon: On it, I'll run the SG change: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0c1d2e --protocol tcp --port 8443 --source-group sg-0b2c3d`
Devon: update applied. Maria: can you test ALB health?
Maria K: Healthchecks are turning green, targets 3/3 healthy. Pods resumed init and started pulling weights.
sre-bot: deploybot: rolling update completed for nodegroup/gpu-pool (2 instances) :white_check_mark: 
Linh: we'll open a quick PR to stop using prefix-list for ALB <-> backend rules and add a NACL pipeline guard. Assigning to @Ashok.
Ashok: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/443 — will add ephemeral egress allow and SG fix tests.
Maria K: thanks all. Logging this as follow-up in incident tracker.
